annotations.text:
Two problems, not one.

The medium was wrong -- stroked vector in a game of PixelGrids. But flat pixel shapes read as diagrams too. The fix is a lit object in a bezel: something to be lit against, and six value steps instead of three.

The frame is code, the object is art.

Bezel, ground, cast shadow and sheen are generated from the talent's category. Forty talents cost forty objects, not forty illustrations -- and one icon is one file, so thirty of them were drawn fourteen at a time.

Proportion, not detail.

SPLIT SHAFT was an axe, then a goblet, then a spanner -- every time because the head was as broad as it was long. LONG REACH was a fountain pen and DEEPER CUT a syringe for the same reason. Looking at all forty on one sheet is what finds these; none of them is visible in the code.

The abstract talents were the hard ones.

FULL TILT is a bigger number and SLIPSTREAM is a rule, not a thing. Both resolve the same way: pick the object the hero HOLDS. A threaded needle goes through without tearing; a wheel cannot be stopped. What never works is drawing the effect.
